preamble: Before front vowels and [j], the labiodental /v/ can be replaced by a voiced alveolo-palatal sibilant [ʑ] as the outcome of labial palatalization. This is the documented result in the northern half of the Moldavian Romanian dialect area, including north-eastern Bessarabia, and in most of Maramureș. Dialectologists transcribe it ź, or z with a note that it is palatal in timbre, unlike primary /z/. Typical forms are zin for standard vin 'wine' and źis for vis 'dream'. The voiceless f undergoes the parallel change to [ɕ]. Southern Moldavia instead shows the older palatal-glide stage, as in yin.

examples.note: The from is the conservative pronunciation with [v], kept in standard Romanian. Recorded in the north-eastern Republic of Moldova, where f, v and ĉ give ś, ź and ś (fier > śer, nuci > nuś).
Recorded in Vicovu de Jos (Suceava); speakers say zin is used more often than vin.
Recorded in Vicovu de Jos and Mănăstirea Humorului; speakers report using the z forms more often than vițel.
Typical of the northern half of Moldavia; south of the Bacău–Vaslui–Huși line, v gives the older glide stage y instead.
The from is the conservative pronunciation with [v], kept in standard Romanian. Found in most of Maramureș; the z that comes from v has a palatal timbre, distinct from primary z.
